findings.summary: The allowed list is the reading's deliverables, not the path the criterion names, so incomplete deliverables make the check refuse files the change needs.
findings.evidence: This job is an example: its plan had to change store.rs, producer.rs and docs/records.md, none of them deliverables. With a limiting criterion it would have been sent back to revert files needed to compile. The user accepted this design, and the CHANGELOG notes that a limiting reading needs a complete deliverable list. Allowing the deliverables plus the planned files would avoid most of these false refusals. The verifier would have flagged the same files later anyway, so this is not a blocker.

findings.summary: The criterion matcher is a keyword-window heuristic and can misfire on sentences that are not scope limits.
findings.evidence: A sentence like 'No file outside the crate changed its API' would match the 'no file … outside … changed' window. The matcher is conservative: its tests reject this job's own criteria, the repository sentences and adjective uses of 'test-only'. A structured reader field would be more exact, but the brief rules out adding one.

summary: The change does what was asked. When an accepted criterion limits which files may change, the job record stores the reading's deliverable paths as a new optional `allowed_paths` field (Job, athena.job/1); older records without it still load. A path-only check (outside_allowed_paths, normalised like normal_path, `dir/` entries cover a tree, deleted files included) runs in producer_loop after each producer report and again at the start of check_and_verify. An outside file is sent back with each path named, the criterion quoted and an instruction to revert it. This send-back is separate from the one for unmet criteria. A file still outside after it closes the job as failed before the checks and the verifier, and retry_findings carries the reason to a retry. A job whose reading has no limit, and a nested run, are not checked. I read the whole diff. The athena-data tests passed when I ran them. I could not run the athena-core tests: every athena-core build here links a stale athena-data library with 24 Job fields, the base version (the source has 25), probably left in the shared target directory by Athena's "fails without the fix" scratch run. A `cargo --config` override to force a rebuild was denied, so I stopped there. For criteria 1–4 I rely on reading the tests plus Athena's recorded CI run for 35ced02, which passed fmt, clippy and `cargo test --locked`; that run includes every new test. Findings are minor: three planned files outside the deliverables list (producer.rs, store.rs, docs/records.md), each needed; the allowed list is the deliverables rather than the path named in the criterion, as the user accepted; and the criterion matcher is a keyword match.
